subject: Dedicated pool saturation causing 5xx and tail latency — Parlay Bank
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@parlaybank.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Cc: parlay-procure@parlaybank.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jan 2029 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden 5xx spike and 200–800ms tail latency on our dedicated pool

Evelyn / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sudden uptick in 5xx errors and high tail latency across our production inference endpoints this morning — both chat and batch embedding paths. Impact started ~07:40 PT. Attached is a screenshot of the 5xx rate and a small sample of request IDs. We're on a dedicated GPU pool with a reserved throughput commitment (monthly).

Immediate questions:
- Do you have visibility on dedicated pool saturation or noisy neighbors right now?
- Are you able to confirm whether our reserved throughput is being honored?
- We need an ETA for mitigation; this is affecting customer-facing flows (loan approvals).

I can be on a call if helpful. Please escalate.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Engineering — Parlay Bank
elena@parlaybank.com
(Attachment: parlay_latency_screenshot.png)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@parlaybank.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jan 2029 08:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx spike and 200–800ms tail latency on our dedicated pool

Elena — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. I'm escalating to ops and the reserved-capacity team now (cc'd).

What I'm doing immediately:
- Opening an internal incident and surfacing the request IDs to infra.
- Asking ops to check dedicated GPU utilization, KV cache pressure, and model kernel errors (OOM / RPC timeouts).
- We will confirm whether your reserved throughput is being throttled or if spillover to shared capacity occurred.

Can you share a sample of request IDs (if not in the screenshot) and confirm whether this is primarily chat generation or embedding traffic? That will help us prioritize the kernel path.

I'll follow up within 30 minutes with a triage note.

— Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(evelyn.hart@redwood.ai)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, elena@parlaybank.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jan 2029 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx spike and 200–800ms tail latency on our dedicated pool

Evelyn / Elena — initial triage from infra:
- Observed sustained GPU utilization >95% on the Parlay dedicated pool (pool-id: p-ded-427).
- Several worker processes hit intermittent CUDA OOMs followed by automatic restarts — correlates with a spike in queued tokens and KV-cache misses.
- There is a long tail of queuing for requests that hit sequence lengths >1024 tokens; batching exploded during a traffic spike.

Immediate mitigations we applied (08:42 PT):
- Temporarily increased burst capacity to the adjacent dedicated cluster to drain queue (30-minute burst authorization).
- Tightened batching cap for high-sequence requests to avoid batch amplification.
- Restarted 3 worker pods with updated kernel flags to favor memory-frugal kernels.

Observed effect (08:55 PT): 5xx rate dropping, median latency improving; tail still elevated for a subset of requests.

Next steps and asks:
1) Recommend enabling prefix KV caching for chat endpoints in your app for the next 24 hours (this will reduce KV miss rate).
2) Ops requests permission to apply a temporary route rule to shift non-urgent batch jobs to the hosted pool for 2 hours to relieve the dedicated cluster.
3) We need PM / procurement input on whether Parlay wants to accept a 1-week temporary burst addendum (SLA amendment) while infra performs a capacity sweep.

Attachments: parlay_logs_20290115.tar.gz (contains sample worker logs and a request-id list).

I'll keep monitoring and will post updated metrics in 15m.

— David Kim
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
(david.kim@redwood.ai)
(Attachment: parlay_logs_20290115.tar.gz)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Jan 2029 09:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx spike and 200–800ms tail latency on our dedicated pool

Looping in leadership for customer / commercial callback. Quick commercial note for the record: Parlay is on a reserved monthly commitment under DEAL-1784 and is sensitive to SLA exposure during month-end processing windows. We need to align on customer communications and whether a temporary credit or burst billing will be offered.

Proposed customer-facing message (to Elena; objective: calm + clear remediation plan):
- Acknowledge impact and confirm we've applied an immediate set of mitigations (burst, worker restarts, batching caps).
- Offer a short-term traffic routing plan (shift non-urgent batch to hosted pool for 2 hours) + a 24–48h root cause window.
- Offer a one-time credit / service rebate to make good if Post-Investigation we confirm the issue is due to reserved-throughput under-provisioning.

Rishi — can you provide a short technical summary we can include in the message?
Evelyn — once we have a concrete timeline for RCA and a billing decision (credit vs temporary burst invoice), I'll draft the external note and standby for sign-off.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success 
(marissa.cole@redwood.ai)
